research_question: What is the effect of prophylactic anticoagulants, compared with placebo or no treatment, on adverse events in non-hospitalised adults with COVID-19 (including outpatients and post-discharge patients)?
outcome_description: Number of participants experiencing at least one adverse event out of the total randomised participants during the follow-up period
positive_direction: A positive effect indicates a lower incidence/risk of adverse events in the anticoagulant arm compared to control (favoring anticoagulation)
search_queries: thromboprophylaxis non-hospitalized COVID-19 adverse events trial
anticoagulation post-discharge COVID-19 placebo controlled trial
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trials evaluating prophylactic anticoagulants (e.g., low-molecular-weight heparin, rivaroxaban, apixaban, aspirin) compared to placebo or no treatment / standard care
Adults with COVID-19 managed in non-hospitalised settings (outpatients or post-discharge patients)
Reporting quantitative participant-level counts of adverse events (any adverse events, serious adverse events, or bleeding events)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, commentaries, and study protocols)
Non-randomised studies, observational designs, or studies conducted exclusively in currently hospitalised COVID-19 inpatients

No comparison between an anticoagulant arm and a placebo or no-treatment control arm (e.g., trials comparing different active anticoagulants or different doses of the same anticoagulant without a control arm)
No usable quantitative participant-level adverse event data (e.g., only reporting total episodes/events without participant counts, or completely unrelated to the research topic)
moderators_to_extract: Anticoagulant drug class and agent (e.g., LMWH, direct oral anticoagulant, aspirin)
Patient population/setting (ambulatory outpatients vs. post-discharge patients)
Adverse event reporting definition (all-cause/any adverse event vs. serious adverse events vs. bleeding events)
Control condition type (placebo vs. open-label standard care/no treatment)
effect_size_note: Pooled as Risk Ratio (RR) using a random-effects model; RR > 1 indicates a higher risk of adverse events in the anticoagulant group.
